story: David Wills was a Gettysburg lawyer. After the Battle of Gettysburg he suggested a national cemetery for the soldiers to Governor Andrew Curtin, who then made him the state's agent to organize it. Because of his work, Abraham Lincoln came to Gettysburg to speak.

Wills invited Lincoln to stay at his house. On November 18, 1863, the night before the ceremony, Lincoln wrote the final draft of the Gettysburg Address in the large upstairs bedroom he was using. During the battle, local people had sheltered in Wills' cellar.
Today the Wills House is a historic house museum operated for visitors.
stops.fact: Lincoln finished the speech the night before he gave it.
stops.disputed: Many people picture Lincoln scribbling the speech in a rush. Wikipedia says he completed the final draft here, in the Wills House, on November 18.

claims.t: Lincoln wrote the final draft of the Gettysburg Address in the Wills House.
claims.why: Wikipedia: the final draft was written in the Wills House on November 18, 1863.

claims.t: Lincoln gave the speech from the steps of the Wills House.
claims.why: He delivered it the next afternoon at the Soldiers' National Cemetery.

story: Pennsylvania Hall, also called Old Dorm, is the central administration building at Gettysburg College and the college's oldest building. John Cresson Trautwine designed it in 1835, and it was built in 1838 in a temple style with four columns in the portico. At first it held students' rooms, offices and classrooms.

When the battle came in July 1863, it was the largest building in town. Union signal officers used its cupola on June 30, and on July 1 a professor led officers up to look out over the area. Soldiers of both armies were treated in the building, nearly 700 of them, until about July 29.
Classes started again on September 24, 1863. The hall was renovated in 1869 and 1870, 1889, and 1928. It is still used for the college's opening and graduation traditions.
stops.fact: It was the largest building in town in 1863.
stops.disputed: Many people think the whole college was a battlefield only. Wikipedia says this building was used as a hospital for both armies.

claims.t: Pennsylvania Hall is the oldest building at Gettysburg College.

claims.t: Only Union soldiers were treated in the building.
claims.why: Soldiers of both armies were treated there.

story: Soldiers' National Monument stands at the central point of Gettysburg National Cemetery. The monument is 60 feet tall, made of granite, and designed by sculptor Randolph Rogers and architect George Keller. The last four lines of the Gettysburg Address are written on it.

A statue of the Genius of Liberty stands on top, and eighteen bronze stars circle the pedestal, one for each Union state with buried dead. Four statues at the corners are War, History, Peace and Plenty, and together they tell a story of peace and plenty after a hard struggle.

The cornerstone was laid on July 4, 1865, and the monument was dedicated in 1869. Many people think it marks where Lincoln gave his speech. Wikipedia says it does not: scholars place the speech about 40 yards east of the monument.
stops.fact: The Genius of Liberty statue was carved in Rome.
stops.disputed: Many people think the monument stands on the exact spot of the Gettysburg Address. Wikipedia says it does not.

claims.t: The monument stands on the exact spot where Lincoln gave the Gettysburg Address.
claims.why: Wikipedia says that is a popular belief but not true.

story: Gettysburg National Cemetery was originally called Soldiers' National Cemetery. It was created for Union soldiers who died in the Battle of Gettysburg, which was fought July 1 to 3, 1863. It has 3,512 Civil War burials, including 979 unknowns, and later sections for veterans of other wars. In all it holds more than 6,000 burials.

On November 19, 1863, four and a half months after the battle, Abraham Lincoln came here to take part in the consecration of the cemetery. His speech has only 271 words, and he read it in less than two minutes to about 15,000 people.
Every year the day of the speech is marked in town as Remembrance Day, with a parade and ceremonies.
stops.fact: The speech was shorter than most of the day's other talks.
stops.disputed: Many people think a famous speech must have been long. Wikipedia says this one has only 271 words and took less than two minutes.

claims.t: Lincoln spoke for more than an hour.
claims.why: Wikipedia says it was read in less than two minutes.
